2813.subject: Government
2813.question_text: The Inspector General of Police is appointed by the executive on the advice of the
2813.explanation:
The Inspector General of Police is appointed by the executive on the advice of the Nigerian Police Council According to 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the functions of Nigeria Police Council include:

1. The organization and administration of Nigeria Police Force and all other matters rating to the thereto (not being matters relating to the use and operational control of the Force or the appointment disciplinary control and dismissal of members of the Force): and

2. The general supervision of the Nigerian Police Force; and

3. advising the President on the appointment of the Inspector General of Police.

2815.subject: Government
2815.question_text: A major problem associated with the Nigerian federalism is
2815.explanation: A major problem associated with the Nigerian federalism is ethnic conflicts. There has been inter ethnic  contact in the various regions but without discrimination and bitter experiences. The issue of neutralization of Lagos in 1953 would have strongly made Chief Obafemi Awolowo to lead the Yorubas to secede from Nigeria but for the threat of war from the Governor and the Colonial office in London. The real secession which was experienced in Nigeria was that of the then Eastern Region in the year 1967. The secession was as a result of the 1966 military coup which was followed by the pogrom that was perpetrated against the Igbos in the North. The East declared the Republic of Biafra and engaged Nigeria in a civil war from 1967-1970. This question of ethnic conflicts has also given rise to other serious issues such has unending demand for creating more states and acceptable revenue allocation formula.

2816.subject: Government
2816.question_text: The six African members of the Nigerian Council were nominated by the
2816.explanation: The six African members of the Nigerian Council were nominated by the governors. The Council was enlarged after the amalgamation so as to cope with the expected increase in problems resulting from increased territory. It was made up of 36 members consisting of the Governor, members of the Executive Council, First Class Residents, Political Secretaries of Northern and Southern provinces as officials. Europeans representing such interests as chambers of Commerce, shipping, banking, mining and six Nigerians nominated by the governor.

2818.subject: Government
2818.question_text: In the Second Republic, the total membership of each House of Assembly was determined by the
2818.explanation:
In the Second Republic, the total membership of each House of Assembly was determined by the Constitution. Going through the Structure of the 1979 Constitution, one should be able to realize that the Constitution was similar to the American Presidential system of government with separation of powers; The legislature, the Executive, etc .
Coming to the noted that the National Assembly was made up of the Senate and the House of Representatives. The Senate was was made up of 450 members 449 have been distributed to the states according to the size and the remaining one being reserved for the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.
Qualified members of the parliament were to be Nigerian citizens up to the age of 30 for the Senate and 21 for the House of Representatives.
Unqualified ones were those with another country's citizenship, lunatics, those under death sentence, undischarged bankrupts, convicts, public servants, etc. The State Assembly was a unicameral legislature which was a unicameral legislature which was made up of Representatives. According to the Constitution, qualified candidates must have attained the age of 21.

2820.subject: Government
2820.question_text: Privatization and commercialization programmes in Nigeria have
2820.explanation:
Privatization and Commercialization programmes in Nigeria have de-emphasized government ownership. This should be clearly seen when we look at the respective definitions of Privatization and Commercialization.

Privatization: This may be defined as the reduction of the burden borne by the government in the provision of goods and services by transferring some of this to the private sector. Full privatization means that government will sell of its controlling shares to the private sector while partial privatization means that reduction of government shares from 60 to 40 percent.

Commercialization: This is the alteration of the capital base of a government company and its modes of operation to enable it engage in business for the sole purpose of making profits.
Companies under full commercialization will no more receive any subvention from the government while those under those under partial commercialization will receive government subvention but will be expected to generate, at least 50 percent of their financial needs from their own operations.

2821.subject: Government
2821.question_text: The fear of domination in the public service led to the
2821.explanation:
The fear of domination in the public service led to the establishment of the Federal Character refers to distribution of amenities and resources or appointments based on quota system. This is to be applied in the three tiers of government in the country. E.G. Political appointments, Location of Unity secondary Schools, Board, Admission into tertiary in institutions, Location of iron tertiary institutions, Location of iron and Steel Mills.

Some of the Factors responsible for the introduction of Federal Characters include:

1. To ensure Unity, Stability, etc.

2. Discrimination

3. Struggle for Lion's share

4. Fear of Domination.

options.text: adoption of population as a formula for revenue allocation
establishment of the Civil Service Commission
establishment of the Federal Character Commission

2823.subject: Government
2823.question_text: In the Igbo political system,the most senior member of the council of elders is the
2823.explanation:
In the Igbo political system, the most senior member of the council of elders is the Okpara. The Igbo political system was based on the village as a political unit.

A village is then seen as made up of a group of related families. Each family head held the Ofo title and all of them put together formed the council of elders. The council of elders governed the village. Among the Ofo title holders, one of them was regarded as the most senior to as the Okpara and he had the right to preside over the council of elders meetings.

2825.subject: Government
2825.question_text: The immediate cause of the 1966 military coup de'etat in Nigeria was
2825.explanation: The immediate cause of the 1966 military coup de'etat in Nigeria was political instability. It should be noted that the Action Group Crises of 1962 was one of the crisis that led to the military take-over of government in January 1966. The 1962 Action Group crisis continued to rear its ugly head, until Western Nigeria election crisis of 1965. The disagreement over the election result between UPGA and NNA in Western region resulted to a crisis which led to a breakdown of law and order. This situation attracted military intervention on 15th January, 1966.

2826.subject: Government
2826.question_text: The exclusive list is reserved for legislation by the
2826.explanation:
The exclusive list is reserved for legislation by the Federal Government. There are about forty three exclusive lists.

Concurrent powers are left for both federal and the state governments while residual lists are reserved for the states only.

2827.subject: Government
2827.question_text: The participation of Nigerians in the Second World War created in the nationalists the awareness that the
2827.explanation:
The Participation of Nigerians in the Second World War created in the nationalists the awareness that the Europeans were not superior.

Their participation in the war, made them to know more about the white people, and realized that they were in no way superior to Africans including Nigerians.

options.text: Africans were more qualified to rule
Europeans were less tactful in warfare

2831.subject: Government
2831.question_text: Which of the following mostly militates against the efficiency and productivity of public corporations in Nigeria?
2831.explanation: Incessant interference by government militates against the efficiency and productivity of public corporations in Nigeria. Sometimes government make them to do things which may not be in the good interest of the corporation.

options.text: The management teams are always appointed at will
members of the management team are always at loggerheads

3031.subject: Government
3031.question_text: The power to nominate members of the judiciary at the federal level under the 1999 Constitution is vested in the
3031.explanation:
The power to nominate members of the judiciary at the federal level under the 1999 Constitution is vested in the National Judiciary Council. According to 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the National Judicial Council shall have power to:-

a. recommend to the President from among the list of persons submitted to it by-

b. the federal judicial service commission persons for appointment to the offices of the Chief Justice of Nigeria, the Justice of the Supreme Court, etc.

c. the judicial service committee of the federal capital territory, Abuja, person for appointment to the offices of the High Court of the federal capital territory, Abuja, etc.

3032.subject: Government
3032.question_text: Prior to 1976,the local government system practiced in Northern Nigeria was
3032.explanation: Prior to 1976, the Local government system practised in Northern Nigerian Nigeria was Chief-in-Council.By 1952, the Northern region abolished the sole Native Authority and put in its place, Chief-in-Council and Chief-and-Council and. The democratization process in the Northern region was further aided by the Native Authority Law of 1954 which was amended by the Northern Nigeria Law of 1963. They provided for five Native Authorities including Chief-in-Council and the Federal Native Authorities.

3033.subject: Government
3033.question_text: In the segmented Tiv society,governance was usually confined to
3033.explanation: In the segmented Tiv society,governance was usually confined to chiefdom . The Tivs were formally traditional worshipers, but some are now Christians. They are ruled by their Chief called Tor Tiv.

3034.subject: Government
3034.question_text: Which of the following influenced nationalist activities in Nigeria?
3034.explanation:
National Congress of British West Africa influenced nationalist activities in Nigeria.

The Congress mobilized educated elites-in-the four British colonies. Other activities of the Congress include:

1. Radical Approach to the National Activities

2. Unification of four West African Colonies

3.Delegation to London

4. Identification of shortcomings

5. Enlightenment of the people of West Africa, etc.

options.text: National Congress of British West Africa

3035.subject: Government
3035.question_text: The party that did not control any state in the Second Republic was
3035.explanation: NAP was the party that did not control any state in the Second Republic. Nigeria Advanced Party (NAP) was not recognized for the 1979 election. The reason was that it was unable to establish branches in 13 states of the federation as stipulated by FEDECO. In the 1983 general elections, which the party contested, it did not win a single seat in all the constituencies.

3036.subject: Government
3036.question_text: Pacification refers to a process through which some areas in Nigeria were acquired by
3036.explanation: Pacification refers to a process through which colonial empires imposed their presence and legal violence through the use of force or military to coerce obedience and subvert the will of the people. It was mainly done in regions impacted and divided by insurgency or rebels.

3037.subject: Government
3037.question_text: Counter-trade was introduced by the government led by
3037.explanation: Counter-trade refers to a system of trade in which goods and services are exchanged partly or wholly instead of using cash, often used to conserve foreign exchange. Counter-trade policies were introduced during the military regime of General Ibrahim Babangida (1985–1993) as part of economic reforms and structural adjustment programs aimed at boosting local production and managing scarce foreign currency reserves.

3038.subject: Government
3038.question_text: A major limitation of the Commonwealth is that it lacks
3038.explanation: A major limitation of the Commonwealth is that, it lacks the power to compel member-nations to comply with its decisions, such as the United Nations Organization (UNO)

options.text: the power to set formal rules to govern the affairs of member nations
an organizational structure and a definite identity
enough funds to run its affairs
the power to compel the member nations to comply with its decisions

3039.question_text: Which of the following countries has withdrawn her membership of the ECOWAS
3039.explanation: The economic Community of West African States was formed on may 28, 1975 by fifteen countries and that was Organization, ECOWAS now stands at fifteen, with the withdrawal of Mauritania, one of the founding members.

3040.subject: Government
3040.question_text: Which of the following is a major threat to OPEC?
3040.explanation:
Development of viable alternatives to crude oil is a major threat to OPEC. For instance, some advanced countries are constantly into research, trying to find an alternative to oil. With this move, the price of oil is negatively affected.

According to Nnoli, 1998 alternatives to oil as source of energy is being discovered day by day, the technologically advanced countries.

As a result, there is an increase in energy efficiency today. For instance, the use of coal, solar, wind, nuclear energy including hydroelectricity has been intensified in the recent years.

options.text: Persistence of war in the Middle East
The discovery of crude oil in more countries
Antagonism by the major world powers
Development of viable alternatives to crude

3041.subject: Government
3041.question_text: The AU's right to intervene in a member country in crisis portrays it as
3041.explanation: The AU's right to intervene in a member country in crisis portrays it as an international organization.

3042.subject: Government
3042.question_text: The permanent membership of the UN Security Council is
3042.explanation:
The permanent membership of the UN Security Council is five.

The 5 permanent members in most cases referred to as the "BIG FIVE" are

1. U.S.A

2. Britain

3. China and

4. The defunct U.S.S.R

3063.subject: Government
3063.question_text: An advantage of flexible constitution is that it allows for
3063.explanation: An advantage of flexible constitution is that it allows for ease of amendment. Changes can be made easily in order to accommodate changing situations in the society. Its amendment does not require or involve much time and financial cost.

3065.subject: Government
3065.explanation: Power refers to the ability to impose one's will upon others. It could also be defined as the ability of a person or a group of persons to enforce his or their decisions on others by the use of sanctions punishment or penalties against disobedience. According to Max Weber, "Power is the capability to control the actions of others"

options.text: ability to impose one's will upon others
duties political parties demand of thir registered memebers
duties an individual imposes on himself

3066.subject: Government
3066.question_text: Prorogation is the bringing of a session of a parliament to an end through
3066.explanation: Prorogation is the bringing of a session of a parliament to an end through royal proclamation. It is termination of a session of the legislature after a period of one year. The president gives his speech after a year before the house resumes. That is after the long vacation.

3067.subject: Government
3067.question_text: The right of all eligible citizens to vote and be voted for is referred to as
3067.explanation:
The right of all eligible citizens to vote and be voted for is referred to as universal suffrage.

Universal suffrage gives voting right to all qualified citizens. But restricted suffrage or restricted franchise restricts voting rights to specified citizens based on age, sex, property, wealth, race or education.

3069.subject: Government
3069.question_text: Values beliefs and orientation of a political system are internalized through
3069.explanation:
Values, beliefs and orientation of political system are internalized through political socialization.

Political socialization is the process by which the citizens are educated on the values, attitudes and belief of the political system.

3073.subject: Government
3073.question_text: Occupational pressure groups pursue their objectives mainly by
3073.explanation: Occupational pressure groups pursue their objectives mainly by pursue their objectives mainly by issuing ultimatums and embarking on strikes. The pressure groups give, 7, 14 or 21 days ultimatum to the government at the end of this, any action which the group deems necessary will be taken against the government. If the demands of the pressure groups are not met at the end of the ultimatum given, they will have to embark on strikes and boycotts.

options.text: issuing ultimatums and embarking on strikes

3075.subject: Government
3075.question_text: In a cabinet system, the legislature comprises of the
3075.explanation:
In a cabinet system, the legislature comprises the prime minister and members of the parliament.

One of the characteristics of cabinet system of government is that the Prime Minister and all cabinet ministers are also members of the parliament or legislature.

options.text: prime minister and members of the parliament
prime minister and members of the jury

3077.subject: Government
3077.question_text: The commitee that scrutinizes budget proposals in the legislature is the
3077.explanation: The Committee that scrutinizes budget proposals in the legislature is the Appropriation Committee.

3081.subject: Government
3081.question_text: Democracy is a system of government that is
3081.explanation:
Democracy is a system of government that is constituted by the will of the majority of the citizens.

It could also be defined as government in accordance with the principles of popular sovereignty, political equality, popular consultation and majority rule. One of the characteristics of democracy is that all government actions must be open to criticisms and must be according to the decisions, wishes and aspirations of majority of the people.

options.text: constituted by the will of the majority of the citizens
imposed on the majority of the citizens
put in place to favour the party caucus

3084.subject: Government
3084.question_text: Collective ownership of property is associated with
3084.explanation:
Collective ownership of property is associated with Communism .

It should be noted that Communism is a social system where the means of production, distribution and exchange are completely owned and managed by the State. The economy is operated centrally and individuals have little or no opportunity for private enterprises.

3087.subject: Government
3087.question_text: The agency responsible for investigating allegations of maladministration in the civil service is the
3087.explanation: The Public Complaints Commission (PCC) is the agency responsible for investigating allegations of maladministration in the civil service and other public institutions in Nigeria. It serves as an ombudsman, handling complaints from the public about injustice, corruption, and administrative inefficiency.

3090.subject: Government
3090.question_text: A political entity that possesses independence is a
3090.explanation:
A political entity that possesses independence is a state.

The state must posses supreme authority within its territory. It must be independent of any foreign control.

3093.subject: Government
3093.question_text: The principle that advocates strict adherence to the fundamental laws of a country is
3093.explanation:
Constitutionalism is the principle that advocates strict adherence to fundamental laws of a country.

This is so when it is well noted that constitutionalism is defined as the principle which maintains that those who govern the society should do so in accordance with the laws of the land. It also means that those who rule the society should follow the stipulations of the constitution strictly.

3095.subject: Government
3095.question_text: One advantage of the unitary system over the federal system is the
3095.explanation: One advantage of the unitary system over Federal System is cost effectiveness. It reduces the cost of running the country. This is because few hands are involved in government.

3096.subject: Government
3096.question_text: Which of the following is a duty of an electoral commission
3096.explanation:
Registration of political parties is a duty of an electoral commission.

Other functions of Electoral Commission are as follows:

a. Division of the country into Constituencies.

b. Registration of voters

c. Determines the type of voting

d. Building of polling booths

e. Provision of Election materials

f. Display and Revision of Voter's Lists

g. Appointment and training of electoral officers

h. Registration of candidates of election

i. Conduct of elections

j. Counting of votes

k. Publishing of election results

l. Enlightens and educates the voters

m. Provision of protection to voters and officials.

n. Disbursement of grants

o. Sees about auditing of accounts.

3099.subject: Government
3099.question_text: A form of government in which the nobles rule for the benefit of all is
3099.explanation:
Aristocracy is a form of government in which the nobles rule for the benefit of all.

This form of government was advocated by some Greek philosophers like Aristotle and Plato who argued that true democracy will depend on the type of citizens a country with wise and just citizens likely to produce good citizens. For this reason, they believed that a country should be governed by the best citizens.

3102.subject: Government
3102.explanation: Fascism as an ideology facilitates Totalitarianism. It is an Italian version of totalitarianism which grew up in Italy under Benito Mussolini

3107.subject: Government
3107.question_text: A prominent feature of a presidential system of government is
3107.explanation: Separation of Power is a prominent feature of a presidential system of government. Separation of powers implies that the three organs of government the Legislature, the Executive and the Judiciary are separated in functions and personnel. In Presidential system of government, the Legislative implements the laws and the Judiciary interprets the laws. There is strict separation of powers in the Presidential system of government.

3110.subject: Government
3110.question_text: The executive checks the excesses of the legislature through
3110.explanation: The executive checks the excesses of the legislature through the use of veto power. The power to veto certain acts of parliament granted to the Executive. President will always make the legislators to sit up.

3111.subject: Government
3111.question_text: The consciousness of a common identity of a people is called
3111.explanation: The Consciousness of a common identity of a people is called nationalism. Nationalism is then defined as the strong emotional awareness of belonging to a nation/state which leads to the struggle against foreign rule of domination.

3123.subject: Government
3123.question_text: Citizenship of a state by descent requires that
3123.explanation: Citizenship of a state by decent requires that one's grandparents were citizens of that state. A child born to a Nigerian couple in the United States of America is a Nigerian citizen by descent because his parents are Nigerians.

options.text: one is born and bred in the state
one's mother was born in the state
one's grand parents were citizens of the state
one is domiciled in that state

3124.subject: Government
3124.question_text: In order to dispense justice impartially, the judiciary primarily needs
3124.explanation: The judiciary needs independence primarily in order to dispense justice impartially. Judges must be free from the absolute control of either the executive or the legislature. That means that the judiciary should not be controlled any how.

3126.subject: Government
3126.question_text: A state with a hegemonic political party is one in which
3126.explanation: A State with a hegemonic political party is one in which there is only one dominant party. In this system, one party is firmly established in office. The party has hegemony, that is, it enjoys unchallenged authority. The law does not operate formally against any opposition, but clearly the state concerned is effectively single-party for longer period of many years. For example, South Africa was an example of a hegemonic party. There, the National party came into power in 1948, and it only left when Dr. Nelson Mandela was elected president in 1994.

3127.subject: Government
3127.question_text: Nigeria's commitment to the liberation of Africa could best be seen in her policy towards
3127.explanation: Nigeria's commitment to the liberation of Africa could best be seen in her policy towards South Africa and Angola. The administration of Murtala Mohammed recognized Agostinho Neto's Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA0 at the expense of US and South Africa's support of UNITA AND FNLA played a decisive role in Angolan independence. In the year 1980, Shehu Shagari's administration offered N10 million to Zimbabwe on their independence celebration while Buhari's administration donated undisclosed amount of money to SWAPO of Namibia and the ANC of South Africa.

3128.subject: Government
3128.question_text: The set of policies on the basis of which countries interact with one another is called
3128.explanation:
The set of policies on the basis of which countries interact with one another is called foreign policy.
It could also be defined as the sum total of decision formulated by the government of a country to manipulate the international environment to attain certain national interest or objective.

3130.subject: Government
3130.question_text: Nigeria's membership of the UN complements her foreign policy in the area of
3130.explanation: Nigeria's membership of the UN complements her foreign policy in the area of multilateral diplomacy.

3132.subject: Government
3132.question_text: Nigeria teamed up with other developing countries to assert a neutral posture under the platform of
3132.explanation:
Nigeria teamed up with other developing countries to assert a neutral posture under the platform of Non-aligned Movement. Non-alignment is the idea or notion of a group of nations in Asia, Africa, Latin America, Caribbean and Europe to be neutral in the cold war between the Western Capitalist and it Eastern Socialist powers.

It should be noted that many African countries have found it difficult to implement the principles of Non-alignment as required. This is mostly due to internal political problems which force them to look for aids and military assistance from either of the blocs. For instance Nigeria and Russia during Nigeria and Biafra war which in most cases referred to as Nigeria civil war.
